messages:
maya: Heads-up — ran into an ambiguity with the matcher today when service-alias patterns + header overrides are present. Behavior flips depending on insertion order. :confused:

maya: Minimal repro (current prod config):
```json
- matcher: host: "*.example.com" -> service: accounts-v1
- matcher: path: "/users/:id" -> service: users
- matcher: header: { name: "x-service", value: "accounts" } + path: "/" -> service: accounts-alias
```

maya: Expected deterministic tie-break (whatever we document). Observed: sometimes the header override wins, sometimes the more-specific path wins.

sam: Ack. This smells like our scoring function not accounting for header anchors consistently. I think we only compute static score for path/host then apply header-based overrides during evaluation which can reorder results non-deterministically if route insertion order differs.

liam: Can you paste the tracer output? route-bot should have the match trace if the endpoint was hit. :eyes:

route-bot: match-trace: candidates:
  - accounts-v1 (score 12, captures 0)
  - users (score 11, captures 1)
  - accounts-alias (score 10 + header-matched)
final: accounts-alias (chosen)

anya: If header matching is applied as a separate pass that adds score at evaluation time, that explains nondeterminism. We should fold header anchors into the static score calculation (or a deterministic tie-break) so order doesn't matter.

maya: Proposal: deterministic comparator with these rules (applied in order):
  1) explicit host exact match > host wildcards (count literal segments)
  2) fewer capture segments preferred (prefer concrete segments)
  3) higher static specificity score (path length + literal weight)
  4) header anchors add a fixed offset to static score (so header presence is baked in)
  5) final tie-break: route creation timestamp (older wins)

sam: +1 to folding header score. Also suggest we expose the computed score in the Console when you hover a route so humans can see why one route outranks another.

liam: UI suggestion: 'Preview match' in the route editor where you can paste a sample request (host, path, headers) and it shows the matched route + scoring breakdown. That will help customers and SREs understand edgecases.

anya: Edgecases: capture vs wildcard: should we treat '*' segment as lower priority than ':id' capture? Currently '*' sometimes beats ':id' because of how we weight length. I propose: literal > named capture > splat/wildcard.

maya: I'll open a small RFC with the comparator rules and a test matrix. Also will add a unit test that permutes insertion order to prevent regressions.

sam: Can we also add a lint in config upload that warns when two routes are within 1 point of each other and differ only by header? That would surface fragile configs.

maya: Good idea. Warns = non-fatal, with a link to the match-preview in Console.

liam: I'll prototype the preview UI. Small note: serialization of the computed score must be stable across language runtimes (we have Go and Rust components). Use integers and avoid floating math.

anya: Implementation note: when folding header anchors into static score, use a fixed integer offset per header condition. Document how offsets stack (e.g., two header matches = +20). Keep offsets conservative to avoid overshadowing path specificity.

route-bot: action: created issue INF-3245 "deterministic-route-comparator + match-preview UI" assigned to maya, sam, liam.

maya: Thanks — will drop the RFC link here once created. For immediate mitigation, we can flip the path that applies header-matching to earlier in the pipeline to make behavior consistent across deploys while we land the comparator change.

sam: Quick follow-up: should canonicalization (trailing slash, case) happen before scoring? I'd say yes. Also record normalized sample in the preview.

maya: Agreed. I'll include normalization steps in RFC.

liam: :thumbsup: I'll start a small frontend branch for the preview, will wire route-bot to show match-trace for any playback hits.

maya: Cool — thanks team.

maya: (later) RFC: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3245/rfc-deterministic-route-comparator — contains comparator matrix + test plan.

sam: Left a comment on the RFC about offsets and metrics to watch (mismatch rate, config warnings).

anya: Added unit test PR draft for wildcard vs capture precedence.

maya: Closing loop: once comparator lands, we'll add telemetry to the Console showing ambiguous-match counts per service. That should reduce support tickets. :white_check_mark:
